title: grace-lin-domain-adaptation-scrapbook-2026-11
content:
Quick brain dump while going through recent domain adaptation/eval papers and jotting ideas for experiments we could run on Redwood workloads. Aim: practical, small experiments that fit into the eval pipeline (fast, interpretable), plus longer term ideas for dataset curation and synthetic-shift probes.

Top-level takeaways (so far):
- Distribution shift is multi-dimensional: covariate shift, label shift, feature collapse from tokenization quirks, and prompt-style/canvas differences (instruction framing). Need to categorize shifts we care about for product teams (hosted-api: user prompts; dedicated/private: enterprise docs; long-context apps: chunking).
- Lightweight probes work: generate controlled synthetic shifts (paraphrase, entity swap, style-shift) and measure gated metrics rather than raw LM perplexity. Per-example evaluation (pass/fail rules) gives better signal for regressions.
- Calibration + selective generation are low-hanging fruit: temperature sweeping + simple confidence thresholds can reduce hallucinations on retrieval-heavy setups.

Papers / short notes: (quick bullets, not exhaustive)
- Paper A: "Contrastive Domain Adaptation for LMs" (arXiv 2023?) — technique: small continued-pretrain on domain corpus + contrastive objective across spans. Observed improvements for NER-style tasks but brittle for generative QA. Thought: try tiny continued-pretrain mixes (1-2M tokens) using customer docs (anonymized) vs public wiki blend; measure delta on RAG QA suite.
- Paper B: "Synthetic Shift Benchmarks" — constructs lexically and semantically shifted evals by controlled insertion/deletion and label remapping. Nice for isolating failures. Could adapt to our developer-facing examples (docs->API, casual->formal).
- Paper C: "Calibration via Temperature Ensembles" — cheap ensemble by sampling temperatures at inference time, then using variance as uncertainty proxy. Seems cheap to implement in Redwood streaming path as an opt-in flag for devs.

Ideas for short experiments (2–5 day cycles):
1) Micro-adaptation: 500k tokens of customer-style docs -> continued pretrain on lightweight infra (1 A10G for a day?). Compare: base model vs micro-adapted model on a small RAG QA set from that customer (sanitized). Metrics: exact-match, faithfulness (hallucination count), generation length. Track cost/time for adaptation and incremental perf.
2) Synthetic-shift harness: add a preprocessor that creates 4 synthetic shifts per evaluation question (paraphrase, numeric format change, entity-swapping, instruction inversion). Run existing eval-suite and compute shift-sensitivity score (std dev of accuracy across shifts). Use as regression metric in rollouts.
3) Confidence plugs: implement temperature-variance wrapper (3 temps: 0.0, 0.7, 1.2) produce 3 outputs, compute token-level log-prob variance -> map to confidence. Use threshold to gate final answer or trigger retrieval re-run. Measure precision/recall on hallucination-labeled set.

Longer experiments / infra needs:
- Build "mini-domain-store" dataset format: small bundles (50–200 docs) with metadata (style, tokenization oddities) that we can deploy to micro-adaptation pipelines. Should live in eval-suite repo (see linked PR).
- Integrate shift-harness into console rollouts: surface shift-sensitivity score per route/model combo. Add a toggle to block canary if sensitivity increases > X%.
- Consider cheap on-the-fly adaptation techniques: LoRA-style adapters trained on a few gradient steps at serving time (maybe in Dedicated/private modes). Need safety guardrails.

Open questions / risks:
- Privacy/regulatory: any customer doc use must be sanitized and KMS-scoped — engineering to make micro-adapt safe in Private deployments. Also, sample leakage across tenants if we mishandle adapter artifacts. Talk to security/legal (cc Ravi).
- Cost vs benefit: micro-adaptation for every tenant is expensive. Need heuristics for when to recommend (high-QPS routes, narrow-domain vocab).
- Metric reliability: synthetic shifts can overfit to transformations we applied. Need to include human-labeled failure sets periodically.

Concrete next steps (this week):
- Prototype synthetic-shift generator in eval-suite (start with paraphrase + numeric-format changes). Owner: Grace (me). PR skeleton to reuse existing evaluation runners.
- Quick micro-adapt pilot with public corpus (e.g., a small law docs scrape) to validate adaptation infra (no customer data yet). Owner: Ravi.
- Slack thread to product-hosted-api outlining potential "adaptation as a product" offering and initial pricing/SLAs (ask PMs for appetite). Owner: Noah to draft.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep experiments reproducible: store seed, tokenizer, pretrain steps, learning rate in eval artifact.
- Try both encoder-only contrastive and generative continued-pretrain objectives; might combine.
- Track wall-clock / GPU-hours for micro-adapt; put into cost model spreadsheet (link to workbook TBD).

Useful links to keep here:
- Synthetic-shift paper (link in linked_artifacts)
- Eval-suite PR (linked_artifacts)
- Short snippet for temperature-ensemble idea: https://gist.github.com/gracelin/temp-ensemble-probe

Random heuristics / heuristics brainstorm (for later doc):
- If shift-sensitivity > 0.12 (stddev normalized) then flag route for "staging-only" rollout.
- Use a combined metric: alpha*exact_match + beta*(1 - hallucination_rate) where alpha=0.7, beta=0.3 when evaluating adaptation effect on QA tasks. Tune later.

Unresolved: how to present adaptation cost to customers in Dedicated? Flat monthly fee + per-MB-adapted? Or offer model variants (adapted vs base) with routing rules. Discuss with commercial.

--- end of quick dump ---
(Will refine into a more formal experiment brief if PMs are interested; want to keep this doc lean and actionable.)
